frs.title: See all concurrent proposals as one set
frs.description: A reviewer can see every concurrent proposal as one comparable set on a single surface, with no paging and no tab-hopping. Realizes UJ-2.
consequences: `GET /proposals` returns every auto-discovered proposal (`agent-*`) in one response; the UI renders all cards at once.
No route-level pagination or collapse exists in v1; a set of N proposals renders as N cards on the canvas.
The set view and the conflict map are visible without opening anything first.

frs.title: Proposal card anatomy
frs.description: A reviewer can judge a proposal from its card: repo name, written intent, stats (`N files`, `+a`, `−d`), and per-file rows. Realizes UJ-1, UJ-3.
consequences: Each card shows `repo`, `intent` when present, file counts, and per-file rows with path + status + additions/deletions.
Cards carry `preview merge` and `Land into demo` actions at rest; file rows carry `view diff`.
Secret-class file rows show the secret badge and key names and offer no diff action.

frs.title: Summary chips (set-level counts)
frs.description: A reviewer can read the set's shape at a glance from five exact counts. Realizes UJ-2.
consequences: On each `/proposals` payload, chips recompute: proposals / shared files / conflicting pairs / changed files / clean pairs.
Tint thresholds: `conflictingPairs > 0` → alert; `sharedFiles > 0` → warn; `cleanPairs > 0` → clean.
Counts are exact and labeled ("N detected", "N active"), never approximate.

frs.title: Collision map (Convergence Conflicts)
frs.description: A reviewer can see which proposals collide, on which files, and where — before reading any diff. Realizes UJ-3.
consequences: For every conflicting pair, the map renders a per-file card: file path, `kind` badge from the conflict-kinds enum, involved repos, and pair rows naming the two repos with base/line regions.
Severity follows the kind mapping (hard conflicts red, `undetermined` amber, clean kinds neutral); cards are read-only with no actions.
The panel meta reads `N detected`; an empty set renders an explanatory empty state, not a blank panel.

frs.title: Freshness cycle
frs.description: The set stays fresh without manual work: pushes appear in seconds, and the surface always converges on the server's truth. Realizes UJ-1, UJ-2.
consequences: `/proposals` refreshes every 8s while auto-refresh is on (default on); a manual `refresh` is always available.
A new top event key (from the ticker) triggers one debounced refresh (500ms).
A land triggers an immediate reload of both `/proposals` and `/events`; within one refresh cycle a landed proposal's card state matches the server.

frs.title: Degradation and errors
frs.description: The surface degrades instead of crashing, and never dresses a failure as success. Realizes UJ-2, UJ-3.
consequences: One error surface: every failed fetch except the ticker funnels into the red Connection banner ("Connection error: {msg}. Retrying..." / "Disconnected from platform worker. Retrying...") with `Retry now`; the banner hides on the next success.
Ticker failure degrades silently — pulse goes stale, last events stay, the rest of the surface keeps rendering.
Action banner: warn in-flight, success/error outcome, dismiss-only (no auto-hide); a new action replaces the previous banner; every failure returns the card to `default`.
The footer sync line (`not synced yet` → `synced HH:MM:SS`) is never error-styled.

frs.title: First-load states
frs.description: A first-time viewer can tell the difference between loading and empty. Realizes UJ-2.
consequences: Chips render `—` until the first payload (today they start at `0`).
Both panels show a loading indicator matching the final layout ("Loading the set from /proposals..." [ASSUMPTION: copy]) and swap to data or empty state on the first response.
The empty states ("No active proposals" / "No convergence conflicts") explain what is awaited.

frs.title: Interaction model
frs.description: Every action is reachable click-first; hover is enhancement, never the only path. Realizes UJ-1, UJ-3.
consequences: Every action is a click/tap on a native control; no drag, no context menus, no custom shortcuts beyond Tab/Enter/Space/Escape.
Inline confirm replaces dialogs: `confirm land?` → commit; `cancel` disarms; no modal confirms, no browser `confirm()`.
Escape closes the topmost modal; backdrop click and `close` do the same; modals stack one level deep.

frs.title: Server-side change-set capture
frs.description: A reviewer can read any proposal's commits, changed files, and diffs without a clone. Realizes UJ-3.
consequences: `GET /changes?repo=…&base=demo&ref=main&baseRef=main` returns the baseline and head identities, stats, and per-file rows.
The change-set carries a per-fork commit list — hash, author, timestamp, message — alongside the per-file rows.
Per-file rows carry status (added/modified/removed), additions/deletions, and a patch; patches are absent for secret, binary, or oversized files.
No read route shells out to git or clones; the review path never clones (architecture: AD-2; the only in-memory clone is inside `/land`).

frs.title: Fork-point diff semantics
frs.description: A proposal's change-set means "what the agent changed" and stays stable while the baseline moves. Realizes UJ-3.
consequences: Change-sets are diffed against the fork point (most recent commit shared with base, first-parent walk limit 200; base-head fallback when none is found).
`/merge` and `/land` use the fork point as the 3-way ancestor (ancestor = fork-point texts, ours = current base head, theirs = proposal head).
After the baseline advances (another proposal lands), an unchanged proposal's change-set is byte-identical.

frs.title: Real conflict detection with enumerated kinds
frs.description: A reviewer can trust that a "conflict" is real — it was produced by attempting the merge. Realizes UJ-3.
consequences: `/proposals` classifies every pair; `kind` ∈ `text-conflict | modify/delete | add/add | undetermined | mergeable | identical-add | both-removed`.
Conflict cards carry the pair's line regions (`base`, `a`, `b` lines) where a region exists.
The summary's `conflictingPairs` / `cleanPairs` counts agree with the map's rendered cards.

frs.title: Diff viewer states
frs.description: A reviewer can read one file's change-set with unambiguous states. Realizes UJ-3.
consequences: Patch rows render additions/deletions/hunk headers with the diff color staff.
A file with no patch renders the placeholder "No patch available for this file (omitted, withheld, or binary)."
Secret content never renders: "Secret content withheld" / "Per platform contract, secret file contents and diffs are never exposed." + key chips.
Error and not-found render distinct badges ("error" / "not found").

frs.title: Merge preview
frs.description: A reviewer can see the landing outcome before committing. Realizes UJ-1, UJ-3.
consequences: `GET /merge` folds the given proposals in order onto the baseline (diff3) and returns `status` `clean|conflict` with per-file action/result.
The modal renders merged text, conflict text with `<<<<<<< / ======= / >>>>>>>` markers, or a withheld notice for secret-class files.
No files changed → "No files changed in merge"; compute failure → "Failed to compute merge".

frs.title: One-click server-side landing
frs.description: A reviewer can land a chosen proposal from its card, with no clone and no CLI. Realizes UJ-1.
consequences: `Land into demo` → inline `confirm land?` → `POST /land`; the worker folds and pushes one commit (`land(<repos>): fold proposal(s)`) to the baseline branch.
In-flight: the card shows a single disabled `landing...` button; the banner narrates "Landing proposal {repo} into {base}...".
The caller needs no local git, no credentials, and never sees a token.

frs.title: Landing outcomes — an open, numbered set
frs.status_raw: built (outcomes 1–5, 7) / build-gap (dedicated `no-changes` banner copy; `withheld-secret` and `conflict` card states) / required-M1 (outcomes 8–9: `stale`, `base-moved`)
frs.description: A reviewer gets an unambiguous outcome for every landing attempt. The set is open and numbered: outcomes 1–7 below, plus 8 (`stale`) and 9 (`base-moved`) — nine total; the last two ship with the land-hardening slice (FR-16, FR-17). Realizes UJ-1 (edge case path).
consequences: `Land into demo` → card flips to `confirm land?` + `cancel` (inline; no dialog).
`confirm land?` → disabled `landing...`; banner (warn) "Landing proposal {repo} into {base}...".

Success → banner (success) "Successfully landed proposal {repo} into {base}. Commit `<sha8>`" — first 8 chars, full SHA in the tooltip; proposals + events refresh immediately; the `repo.pushed` event re-enters the ticker.
409 `withheld-secret` → error banner "Withheld-secret file — landing blocked ({files})."
409 `conflict` → error banner "Conflicted files: {files}. (preview merge first)"
409 `no-changes` → dedicated variant: "Nothing to land — fold produced zero changes." [ASSUMPTION: copy]
Any other failure → error banner "Failed to land {repo}: {msg}".
409 `stale` → error banner "This proposal is stale — rebase and re-push to land." [ASSUMPTION: copy]
409 `base-moved` → error banner "Nothing to land — the baseline moved since this proposal was made." [ASSUMPTION: copy]
Every failure returns the card to `default`; the banner persists until dismissed; card states for `withheld-secret` and `conflict` are specified in the UX spine and not yet rendered (build gap).

frs.title: Reviewed-state precondition
frs.status_raw: required-M1 — planned (land-hardening workstream; contract bump first)
frs.description: A reviewer can trust that what lands is what was reviewed. Realizes UJ-1.
consequences: `/land` accepts the reviewed base head and proposal heads (additive request fields) and returns 409 `stale` on mismatch — no silent re-fold.
Landing content a reviewer never saw is impossible through the public route once the precondition is enforced.

frs.title: Concurrency precondition
frs.status_raw: required-M1 — planned (land-hardening); the DO lease arrives later (roadmap, unsequenced)
frs.description: Concurrent landings cannot silently overwrite each other. Realizes UJ-1.
consequences: After the in-memory clone, `/land` re-reads the base head and returns 409 `base-moved` on divergence.
A Durable Object lease (roadmap, unsequenced) serializes lands when it arrives; until then the precondition is the guarantee.
The race is reproduced and covered by a regression check (4 concurrent lands → no silent overwrite).

frs.title: Landing record and validation evidence
frs.status_raw: required-M1 (land-hardening workstream); the short-SHA receipt is the minimum the build carries today
frs.description: Every landing is traceable and carries its validation evidence: what was reviewed, what checks ran and their results, what was folded, and the hash that proves merged-SHA equals tested-SHA. Realizes UJ-1.
consequences: Every landing records ancestor + heads + fold hash; merged-SHA-equals-tested-SHA is checked against the recorded fold hash — no landing claims validation it did not run.

The landing record extends with `evidence { checks[], results[], mergedSha, testedSha, artifactRef, at }` on `POST /land`; a read surface serves the record — planned route `GET /landings/{commit}`. [ASSUMPTION: the contract bump is pinned with the land-hardening workstream per contract-first discipline (FR-42) — the latest `CONTRACT.md` revision carries it.]

The short-SHA success banner is the minimum receipt, not the target; the evidence artifact ships with the land-hardening workstream (Milestone 1). `landed.files` and `landed.at` render in the same slice (contract-defined, currently unrendered — build gap).
The decision record persists as a git note on the proposal.

frs.title: Landed-state card
frs.description: A reviewer can see at a glance that a proposal has nothing pending. Realizes UJ-1.
consequences: `landing.status === "landed"` (or `stats.files === 0`) dims the card to 0.55 opacity with a dashed border and the "landed — nothing pending" line ("All changes from this branch have been merged into baseline.").
`landing.status` is content-derived: a zero-change fold is `landed`; `/land` with zero changes is 409 `no-changes` — never a fake success.

frs.title: Events ticker
frs.description: A reviewer can see recent platform activity without asking. Realizes UJ-1, UJ-2.
consequences: The ticker shows the newest ≤8 events (type, repo, time); it consumes the real-time feed (FR-22) and polls `/events` every 2s only on the fallback path.
A push appears in the ticker within seconds and can trigger the debounced proposals refresh (FR-5).
On `/events` failure the pulse goes stale and the last events stay; the ticker never breaks the rest of the surface.

frs.title: Event feed discipline
frs.description: The event feed is accurate: recorded once, deduped, validated, and never authoritative for writes. Realizes UJ-1.
consequences: Artifacts events arrive through exactly one queue consumer (the worker) — the sole recorder; dedupe key `(type, repo, ref, after)`.
Events without repo identity are logged and dropped, never partially recorded; payloads are validated (type whitelist, repo/ref charsets, hex shas) before recording (sequenced M2).
`GET /events` serves the ≤50 newest; KV `LIVE` has exactly one writer; the feed is a hint, never authority for writes or identity.

frs.title: Real-time transport, polling fallback
frs.description: The UI is event-driven end to end: pushes, forks, and landings surface in real time; polling exists only as the degraded fallback. Realizes UJ-1, UJ-2. [OQ-3 (retired) — real-time required, 2026-10-06.]
consequences: Real-time transport (SSE or WebSocket over a Durable Object hub) carries platform events to the UI; a push appears without any poll, and a landing updates the set without waiting for a refresh cycle.
The proof form holds: on-screen freshness visibly beats a 90 s poll (SM-2 keeps the ≤2 s form), captured as demo evidence.

Polling remains the degraded fallback: when the transport is unavailable, `/events` 2s, `/proposals` 8s (auto-refresh toggle, default on); a land reloads both endpoints immediately; `/events` failure must never break the proposals UI.
As-built today: polling only (the event pipeline is live); the real-time transport ships in Milestone 1.

frs.title: Three typed card signals
frs.description: A reviewer can see three advisory signals per proposal: risk, intent-vs-diff, semantic collision. Realizes UJ-3.
consequences: `POST /judge` `setId v1` returns one typed entry per judged proposal: `risk.label` ∈ {routine, focused, senior-security} + `risk.score` [0,2]; `intent.verdict` ∈ {supports, contradicts, insufficient} + `intent.overclaim` [0,1] (null when insufficient); `collision` boolean.
Unknown `setId` → 400 `unknown-set`; sets are versioned in code; new ids are additive and existing ids never change meaning.
The wire carries typed answers, never prose; thresholds, weights, and labels live in code.

frs.title: Server-assembled state, pinned model, fail-closed
frs.description: A reviewer can trust that judgments cannot be steered from the outside and never appear when the judge is unavailable. Realizes UJ-3.
consequences: Callers cannot supply `state`, `questions`, or `model`; unknown fields → 400 `bad-request`.

State is assembled server-side from the same fork-point change-sets the set view uses; untrusted content enters delimited and labeled as data; instruction-like text is stripped; every outbound state passes the masking filter (no secret-class values).

Model id is pinned (`@cf/cloudflare/clef`); a response whose `model` differs or is absent ⇒ 503 `judge-unavailable` (no judgments); schema-invalid answers ⇒ 503; failures are silent to the UI and never block landing.

Per-caller caps: 60 judge runs/min and 1000/day; beyond → 429. [ASSUMPTION: constants proposed — pin in code at the land-hardening slice.] `skipped[]` lists unjudged proposals with reasons (`secret-class`, `empty-change-set`) — a skip is not a verdict.

frs.title: Advisory chip rendering
frs.description: A reviewer can read judge output as advice, visibly distinct from hard conflict state. Realizes UJ-3.
consequences: Chips render on proposal cards in the existing badge/chip language; collision emphasis introduces no new hues; advisory signals stay amber/neutral and are never dressed as a red hard conflict.
Skipped proposals render no chips.
"The judge advises; code decides; humans still own irreversible acts" holds in behavior: no chip blocks or forces an action.

frs.title: Auto-land gate
frs.status_raw: roadmap (unsequenced — the judge is live; the gate is explicitly not engaged, pending calibration per FR-27/OQ-5)
frs.description: Auto-landing can exist later, gated and fail-closed — not before. Realizes UJ-1. *[NON-GOAL: engaging auto-land — the gate is roadmap, unsequenced (OQ-5); no demo or first-version path auto-lands.]*
consequences: The gate is evaluated inside `POST /land` before fold and push; when engaged and the judge cannot answer, `/land` fails closed (no push).
Auto-land stays off until an injection-testing spike passes on our labeled set and at least one non-model corroborating signal exists (fold status / conflict map).
Clients render verdicts; they never decide them.

frs.title: Calibration before trust
frs.status_raw: required-M1 (advisory-only; the gate stays off) — calibration not yet run; the judge ships advisory-only until the calibration record exists
frs.description: Judge thresholds are tuned on our own labeled proposals before any gating is trusted.
consequences: The calibration record's minimum contents: ≥50 labeled proposals carrying risk + intent-verification labels; precision ≥0.9 on the ship-blocking class; the injection-testing spike passes; sign-off by John. [ASSUMPTION: numeric targets proposed.]

Thresholds/weights/labels are code constants tuned on that labeled set; the first version ships advisory-only until the record exists — the auto-land gate engages only after the record exists (OQ-5 cites this).
Model id is logged per response; drift to an unpinned id fails closed.

frs.title: Secret-class masking law
frs.description: A reviewer can read a secret-class file's schema without exposing a value. Realizes UJ-1, UJ-2.
consequences: Secret-class paths (`.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `*.p12`, `credentials.json`, `secrets.json`, `.dev.vars`, any path containing `secrets/`) render key names only (`keys[]`) in any response body — never values; secret rows carry no patch and no intent.
No secret-class content leaves the worker in any form — including logs and any AI/judge state; outbound judge states are constructed through the masking filter.
Free-text channels derived from repo content (intent, notes, error strings) are scrubbed: `KEY=VALUE`-shaped values redacted; intent dropped whenever the head commit touches a secret-class path.

frs.title: Blocked landing and withheld merges
frs.description: A reviewer cannot leak a secret by landing it. Realizes UJ-1.
consequences: A fold touching a secret-class file returns `withheld-secret`; `/land` with any affected secret-class file → 409 `withheld-secret` with the files listed; values are never pushed by the worker.
Merge previews render `result: withheld-secret` with the withheld notice and no text.

frs.title: Masking posture and widening
frs.description: Masking is path-driven by design in this version; widening is deliberate, additive, and decided once.
consequences: A secret value placed in a non-secret-class path is not redacted in v1 (documented limitation; values must live in secret-class paths).
Widening the class list is additive via a contract bump.
Content-detected secrets (non-path) arrive either as a contract-bumped additive status value or as a judge gate — decided once in `CONTRACT.md` before that unit ships, never implicit.

frs.title: Elevated reveal
frs.status_raw: sequenced (M2) (requires the auth seam and the §7.5 auth decision gate; not demo-able before them)
frs.description: Masked-by-default holds everywhere until an authorization mechanism exists. [OQ-2 (retired) — sequenced to Milestone 2 behind the auth seam.] *[SEQUENCED: elevated reveal — Milestone 2, behind the auth seam and the §7.5 auth decision gate. The demo shows schema-only views and the withheld notice; no value-reveal surface ships before the seam is enforced.]*
consequences: No route or view exposes secret-class values today; the schema-only view and the withheld notice are the complete surface.
Elevated reveal requires the auth seam plus an explicit authorization rule; until then it does not exist anywhere in the product.

frs.title: Intent records via the notes mirror
frs.description: Every change-set can carry its why, durably. Realizes UJ-1, UJ-3.
consequences: Intent lives as git notes pushed to `refs/notes/commits` and mirrored to branch `nextgit-notes` in one push (three refspecs); all readers use the mirror; fallback carrier `NEXTGIT_INTENT/<sha>.txt` lives only on the mirror.
Exactly one pusher per proposal repo — the runner/orchestrator performs the push after commit; agents never push refs; the mirror is fast-forward-only.
Intent survives a rebase and is visible on the card (`intent`) and file rows.

frs.title: Provenance visible
frs.description: A reviewer can see where a change came from and what was decided. Realizes UJ-2, UJ-3.
consequences: Cards show the proposal repo and the baseline (`base: demo · ref: main` in the header).
The landing decision record persists as a git note (FR-18) and a `repo.pushed` event records the baseline move in the feed.

frs.title: Provision N isolated workspaces
frs.description: An operator can provision N isolated agent workspaces from one baseline in one command. Realizes UJ-1.
consequences: One command creates N forks with scoped tokens; each accepts independent pushes; each push emits an event.
Provisioning guarantees discoverability before tokens are handed off (conventions naming, status ready); auto-discovery semantics are documented in the contract.
Demo floor: N≥4 real agents proven concurrently.

frs.title: Harness onboarding and routing
frs.status_raw: built (omp + codex verified) / pending (more harnesses via routing)
frs.description: An operator can onboard real agent CLIs — starting with omp and codex — and bring their own harness. Realizes UJ-1.
consequences: omp and codex routes produce real proposals against the baseline (verified; claude/gemini/opencode are standing auth items, not blockers).
BYO harness is supported through the standard interface: agents edit their own clones; the runner/orchestrator commits and performs the single three-refspec push; agents never push refs.
The platform ships a machine-readable tool manifest + structure map into every workspace (engineering law: no context-blind agents).

frs.title: Token lifecycle
frs.description: Credentials are short-lived, scoped, audited, and never rendered. Realizes UJ-1.
consequences: Worker-minted access tokens: single-use, TTL ≤300 s, revoked in a `finally` (as-built today). Repo git tokens: 24 h default, 7 d max. [ASSUMPTION: repo git token TTLs proposed.]

Token values live mode 0600 outside repos/transcripts, never in logs or argv; mint/use/revoke are audited at two surfaces: Worker logs (observability) and Artifacts token events (`token.created` / `token.revoked`).
No response ever contains tokens or credentials (architecture AD-9; the law holds today even though the seam is sequenced (M2)).

frs.title: The 10-step interactive tour
frs.description: A first-time viewer can learn the model in one sitting, without documentation. Realizes UJ-4.
consequences: The tour ships 10 clickable stepper tabs (0. Intro … 9. Your Role) with progress fill; narrow widths scroll the stepper horizontally.

Steps 0–5 teach with simulations; step 6 fetches and renders the real `/proposals` grid inside the tour, annotating real collisions, clean additions, and landed changes; step 7 quizzes over the real proposal set; step 8 states non-goals; step 9 frames the operator and offers `Open the Triage App`.

frs.title: Tour degradation
frs.description: The tour never breaks and never shows an error banner. Realizes UJ-4.
consequences: Step 6 fetch failure → console warning + graceful fallback snapshot; the tour continues.
The tour is the mobile-friendly member of the family (single-column stacking at ≤720px).

frs.title: Reproducible end-to-end demo
frs.description: An operator can reproduce the demo end-to-end from committed scripts.
consequences: Committed scripts: `seed.mjs` (baseline) · `agents.mjs` (scripted) · `real-agents.mjs` (REAL CLI agents) · `land.mjs` (lands or refuses) — reproducible from the repo.
The run shows N≥4 real agents concurrently, ≥1 genuine collision surfaced pre-land, one-click landing with receipt, secret masking and provenance visible.
No mocks: live Workers + Artifacts end to end.

frs.title: Rehearsed failure paths
frs.status_raw: built (spec'd; rehearsed as part of the demo run)
frs.description: The demo (and the product) handles its failure modes with exact copy. Realizes UJ-1.
consequences: Colliding land → 409 conflict, files named, "(preview merge first)"; secret-touching land → 409 withheld-secret; any other failure → generic error.
Every failure returns the card to `default`; the banner stays until dismissed.

frs.title: Submission package
frs.description: The entry can be submitted and judged.
consequences: Deliverables: a 5–10 minute video; an open-source repo (MIT/Apache/BSD + LICENSE file); run instructions.
The demo is one uninterrupted take exercising all three rubric axes (originality/prototype 50%, multi-agent concurrency 25%, UX 25%) on real infrastructure; single entry.

frs.title: Contract discipline
frs.description: Any client can depend on shapes that never drift silently.
consequences: `platform/CONTRACT.md` is the single source of route shapes; changes are additive-only; a shape change bumps the contract first.
Every new route or payload lands its shape in `CONTRACT.md` in the same slice that adds it — no producer or consumer ships an undocumented shape.
Default resolution of `base`/`ref`/`baseRef` is identical on every route and pinned; every API route enforces its method; unknown API paths return JSON 404 (never asset fallthrough).

frs.title: Route surface
frs.description: A client can drive the whole platform through the documented route surface.
consequences: Routes: `GET /health`, `GET /changes`, `GET /proposals`, `GET /merge`, `POST /land`, `POST /judge`, `GET /events`; errors are `{ ok: false, error }` with 4xx/5xx.
Enums are frozen where documented: file status, conflict kinds, landing status; commit messages `land(<repos>): …`; timestamps ISO-8601 UTC.
`/judge` is contract-pinned and rate-limited per caller; `target.repos` ≤16; `refs` exactly one entry in v1.

frs.title: Client protocol for future surfaces
frs.status_raw: sequenced (M4) (second client); the 11-entity protocol is pending
frs.description: A future client — Agent Office, IDE, CLI — can render and act on platform state from the API alone; the second client is the API's proof. *[SEQUENCED: shipping a second client — Agent Office and IDE/CLI surfaces arrive in Milestone 4; the API is built for them.]*
consequences: The 11-entity protocol (Floor/Project, Worker, Task/Queue, Issue, Pull/Proposal, Pull/Proposal detail, Presence/Peer, Whiteboard, Services, Settings, Chat/Notifications) plus the contract-pinned push-event surface is the client contract.
GitHub-specific semantics (`reviewDecision`, `mergeStateStatus`, `mergeable`) are synthesized in adapters — never in the core.
A second client (e.g., the 3D office) renders live platform state without platform changes; this is an adoption signal, not a v1 build target.

frs.title: Auth seam
frs.status_raw: sequenced (M2) (seam wave; hard precondition before non-demo data; the §7.5 auth decision gate precedes it)
frs.description: The platform is auth-ready and demo-open, with zero credential egress.
consequences: A single `authorize(request, env, action, {repo|base})` chokepoint is called by every route; `AUTH_MODE` defaults to deny; the demo opts in explicitly (`demo`).
While demo, a repo allowlist (`demo`, `agent-*`) is enforced on every `base`/`repos` param; edge rate limits cover `/land`, `/merge`, `/proposals`, `/judge`.
The seam is enforced before the first non-demo data exists in the namespace; CSRF protection is required for the future cookie-based SSO path.

frs.title: Declare intent before building; match it against the fork ecosystem
frs.description: A builder can declare intent before building and match it against the fork ecosystem — joining existing work instead of restarting it.
consequences: The matcher returns one verdict per declared intent — `merge-it` (an existing fork already carries the work), `use-as-context` (overlap supplies context), or `ignore` (no actionable overlap).
Fork cards carry the six-cluster signals that drive matcher verdicts (defined in `fork-community.md`, the CAP-10 companion).
Join-don't-restart is a platform reflex: the default path from a declaration leads to the fork that already attempted the work, not to a restart.
Merge-back-to-upstream paths are defined: a fork's work can be routed back to the repository it forked from.

frs.title: R2 asset tier
frs.status_raw: sequenced (M3) (R2 tier in product scope; OQ-1 resolved 2026-10-06)
frs.description: A repo can carry large and binary assets without bottlenecking the git fabric: assets are content-addressed blobs in R2; git carries manifests and pointers only.
consequences: Large/binary assets are stored as content-addressed blobs in R2, and the repo holds a manifest/pointer (path, blob id, content hash, size) in Artifacts — clones, change-sets, and the fork-point contract are unchanged.
Integrity verification: a blob whose content hash does not match its pointer fails closed — no silent substitution; verification runs on any read path that materializes a blob.
Lifecycle: bucket lifecycle rules (retention/expiry) plus lifecycle-safe deletes — removing a path removes the pointer and schedules the blob; no orphan-blob accumulation.
Git is NOT re-architected for blobs: the five landing semantics, secret masking, and the fork-point change-set contract are unchanged — the tier adds a pointer layer only.

nfrs.title: Compute envelope
nfrs.text: All change-set, conflict, and merge-preview work happens in-Worker within the Workers CPU budget: 30 s default / 5 min max per HTTP request. No read route clones; the only in-memory clone is inside `/land` (AD-2). Fork walks are bounded at 200 first-parent commits.

nfrs.title: Artifacts envelope
nfrs.text: 1 GB/repo · 32 MB/file · 2k git requests/10 s/repo; push cap ~64 MiB → small incremental pushes; push protocol v1-only. Artifacts provides no server-side merge, diff, conflict detection, or branch protection — the platform builds all of them (SPEC constraints).

nfrs.title: Runtime pin
nfrs.text: One Worker (`nextgit-platform`); compatibility date 2026-09-01; no `nodejs_compat` (in-tree fs/Buffer shims). Deploys use the lockfile-pinned local wrangler, never `@latest`. Worker logs never include Authorization headers or request bodies.

nfrs.title: One gated write path
nfrs.text: The worker performs no git writes except the single-commit fold+push inside `POST /land`; base branches are written only by `/land`; control-plane pushes are limited to provisioning baselines and proposal repos; landing replays are prohibited (AD-1).

nfrs.title: Secret egress law
nfrs.text: No secret-class content leaves the worker in any response, log, or model state; free-text channels derived from repo content are scrubbed before entering any body (AD-4).

nfrs.title: Zero credential egress
nfrs.text: No response ever contains tokens or credentials — no exception; failure paths return fold artifacts only; no response carries shell snippets containing repo content or paths (AD-9).

nfrs.title: Single writer / single consumer
nfrs.text: KV `LIVE` has exactly one writer (the worker); the queue has exactly one consumer; Artifacts events are deduped on `(type, repo, ref, after)`; the feed is a hint, never authority for writes or identity (AD-6).

nfrs.title: Degrade, never fake
nfrs.text: Every failed fetch except the ticker surfaces in one connection banner; panels keep their last render; the ticker degrades silently; landing state is content-derived — the UI never shows a success it did not observe.

nfrs.title: Accessibility floor (WCAG 2.2 AA behavioral floor)
nfrs.text: Visible focus on every interactive control; modal focus trap returning focus to the trigger; Escape/backdrop/close modal semantics; reduced-motion support; ≥44px touch targets at phone widths; document-order tab order. Known gap to fix: `{colors.text-muted}` ≈3.3:1 and `{colors.text-dim}` ≈2.1:1 are below 4.5:1 for small text — confined to meta labels/ambient chrome; they must not be extended to body copy or state messaging, and raising them is a pending decision. [ASSUMPTION: floor ratified for M1 (revisit at the §7.5 gate; John may overrule anytime).] [NOTE FOR PM: raising `{colors.text-muted}`/`{colors.text-dim}` is a pending decision — the current ratios are the as-built floor, not a ratified contrast target.]

nfrs.title: Concerns floor
nfrs.text: Dark-only theme; desktop-web primary; English-only copy; no offline, no native, no PWA. [ASSUMPTION: ratified for M1 (revisit at the §7.5 gate; John may overrule anytime).]

nfrs.title: Contract-first
nfrs.text: Additive-only shapes; bump before change; defaults pinned in `CONTRACT.md`; consumers read only documented surfaces (AD-8).

nfrs.title: Design constitution
nfrs.text: Every requirement's intent answers to the twelve engineering laws (`engineering-laws.md`; per-law carrier mapping: `reconcile-spec.md` §3); laws not yet carried as FRs ride as roadmap explicitly — L2 two-tier intelligence (fast System-1 sweeps classify every file before expensive reasoning), L9 work-item ↔ change-set linkage, L11 always-on decision layer; the partially-represented laws remain binding.

GAP #6 — judge chips + auto-land gate planned P0, not rendered: risk score, intent-vs-diff verification, semantic collision; when built: chips on the card, gate behind the Land button; "the judge advises; code decides; humans still own irreversible acts." GAP #7 — <424px overflow: proposals grid 360px track floor + 2rem container padding overflows below ~424px viewports; fix = single column below the floor `[ASSUMPTION]` (`EXPERIENCE.md:259`). Triage app has no authored media queries; only tour.css has breakpoints (768px, 640px) (`EXPERIENCE.md:255-257`).

Pending-intake state behaviors to lock at requirement level: WCAG 2.2 AA floor; tab order; modal focus trap; reduced-motion; 44px touch targets; first-load treatment; card treatments for the two unrendered states; `no-changes` copy (`EXPERIENCE.md:264`).

Interaction requirements as behavior: click-first (no drag/context menus/custom shortcuts beyond Tab/Enter/Space/Escape); inline confirm replaces dialogs; Escape closes topmost modal (one level deep, never two); hover is enhancement only — every action always visible without hover; tab order = document order, modal traps focus and returns it to trigger `[ASSUMPTION — verify in build]` (`EXPERIENCE.md:32`, `:177-181`).

Polling cadence is behavioral requirement, not implementation detail: `/events` 2s; `/proposals` 8s with toggle on; new top event debounce 500ms; land reloads both endpoints; `/events` failure must never break proposals UI; push-style immediacy is the product goal — as-built polls (`EXPERIENCE.md:182`). Set view, no paging — all proposals on one canvas, no tab-hopping, no collapse (`EXPERIENCE.md:183`).
Provenance requirement: the landing decision persists as a git note (`EXPERIENCE.md:214`).

arch_constraints.text: CPU budget: Workers CPU 30 s default / 5 min max per HTTP request; all change-set/conflict work in-Worker diffs, no server-side git (SPINE:69; SPEC:53).

Artifacts limits: 1 GB/repo · 32 MB/file · 2k git req/10 s/repo; no server-side merge/diff/conflict/branch-protection — the platform builds them (SPEC:51); 32 MB/blob wall stands (MEMLOG:21). Push ~64 MiB cap → small incremental pushes; push protocol v1-only (SPEC:52).
Runtime pin: compat 2026-09-01, no `nodejs_compat` (in-tree fs/Buffer shims) (SPINE:162,135); isomorphic-git ^1.43.0 (v1 wire; SPEC names 1.42.x — verified compatible REAL:53).
Environments: one environment (live demo `nextgit-platform.john-b7d.workers.dev`); no staging split until auth seam + non-demo data (SPINE:177,251).
Fork walk limit 200 on change-set diffing; landing preconditions `stale`/`base-moved` (SPINE:75).

Events/polling plan: `/events` ≤50 newest; KV single writer; queue single consumer; dedupe `(type,repo,ref,after)`; polling only as fallback (SPINE:93); live-feed transport (SSE/WS) deferred until polling latency is real at scale (SPINE:253).

Scale budget unresolved: `/proposals` fully recomputes per poll; only AD-2's CPU sentence bounds it; a P2 cache item is the implicit home (RUB:33); brief flags the 20–50-proposal fleet view as a known engineering budget item (BRIEF:64).
Token lifecycle: worker tokens minutes-TTL, single-use, revoked in `finally`; agent tokens hours-scale; 0600 outside repos/transcripts; never logs/argv; mint/use/revoke audited (SPINE:99).
Auth/demo: `AUTH_MODE` default deny; demo allowlist `demo`/`agent-*`; rate limits on `/land`,`/merge`,`/proposals`,`/judge`; seam enforced before first non-demo data (SPINE:111).
Judge: pinned model, fail-closed, per-caller budget/rate caps, auto-land requires injection-spike pass + non-model corroboration (SPINE:123).
Deploy/log hygiene: lockfile-pinned wrangler only; worker logs never Authorization headers or request bodies (SPINE:135).
Gate rule: 0 ship-blockers + 0 highs; contract smoke in each platform VERIFY (SPINE:129).
Write protection is ours to enforce: CF `read_only:true` flag does NOT constrain binding-level writes (probe landed on a read-only fork) — never assumed as a guard (MEMLOG:39).
No Windows/GPU/macOS hosting; no servers to run; only local dependency is the loop host (SPINE:147,177).

Auth seam v1 + token lifecycle (P1) (SPINE:107-111; MEMLOG:34).
Secret-class widening + scrub (P1) and the content-scan decision landing in CONTRACT before its unit ships (SPINE:81).
Contract smoke in VERIFY gates + `tsc --noEmit` type gate (`contract-smoke-verify-gates` P2) (SPINE:129; MEMLOG:34).
Client contract: CONTRACT.md + 11-entity protocol + push-event surface; adapter synthesizes GitHub semantics (SPINE:137-141; capability map SPINE:226-237: CAP-1..10, CAP-10 deferred).
